rules.label: A first professionally qualifying degree in Computer Science (Informatik) or a related study programme

check.note: TU Berlin's examination board decides whether your first degree is Computer Science or a related programme and equivalent to a German degree (R01). A matching degree title does not settle it.

citations.quote: The specific admission requirement is a first professionally qualifying degree in the field of “Informatik” or Computer Science or in a related study program.

rules.label: At least 36 credits in the foundations of computer science (the three areas below together)

citations.quote: 36 CP in foundations of computer sciences, including 12 CP in the field of Theoretical Computer Science

rules.label: At least 12 credits in Theoretical Computer Science (formal languages, automata, computability, complexity, logic)

citations.quote: 12 CP in the field of Theoretical Computer Science
Theoretical Computer Science includes courses i.e. on the topics formal languages, automata, computability, complexity, logic.

rules.label: At least 12 credits in Computer Engineering or Information Technology

citations.quote: 12 CP in the field of Computer Engineering or Information Technology

rules.label: At least 12 credits in Methodological and Practical Computer Science

citations.quote: 12 CP in the field of Methodological and Practical Computer Science
18 CP in the field of Mathematics

rules.label: At least 30 further credits in computer science, not counting your thesis, on top of the credits above

citations.quote: at least 30 CP in the field of computer sciences, not including your thesis

rules.label: The examination board decides which of your modules count for each subject area

check.note: The examination board decides the equivalence and which modules fall in which area (R12). Discrete structures, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, digital logic and design and analysis of algorithms do not count as Theoretical Computer Science. Foreign credits are converted to ECTS by the board if needed. The credits you entered are your own allocation.

citations.quote: The responsible examination board decides on the equivalence and the subject-specific qualification.
Courses on discrete structures, discrete mathematics, algorithms, data structures, digital logic, design and analysis of algorithms are not recognized in the field of Theoretical Computer Science

rules.label: Proof of English above B2: IELTS overall 6.5, or a completed degree from a native-English country

children.note: Other certificates on the Faculty IV list of accepted English proofs (CEFR level above B2) are not captured in the cached pages and the profile has no generic English level; TU Berlin decides. IELTS 5.5 is not enough even if it shows B2.

citations.quote: For the IELTS test, an overall band score of 6.5 is required, even if an overall band score of 5.5 confirms a B2 on the certificate.
A successfully completed degree at a university will only be recognized as proof of English proficiency if it meets our definition of “native English.”
Please note that a higher B2 English level is required.

rules.label: VPD from uni-assist for a first degree from a foreign university (applications from summer semester 2026)

citations.quote: will need a preliminary review documentation (VPD) for their application to TU Berlin from the summer semester of 2026 onwards.

rules.label: Suitability Assessment Form (needed unless your bachelor's was in Computer Science at TU Berlin)

citations.quote: you will need to add the Suitability Assessment Form to your application documents.

rules.label: IELTS section (component) scores: no minimum is published, only the overall band

check.note: TU Berlin publishes an IELTS overall band of 6.5 and no minimum per section.

citations.quote: For the IELTS test, an overall band score of 6.5 is required, even if an overall band score of 5.5 confirms a B2 on the certificate.
